title: European Stroke Organisation (ESO) and European Association of Neurosurgical Societies (EANS) guideline on stroke due to spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage
shortTitle: ESO/EANS 2025: ICH care without premature prognostic limits
source: European Stroke Organisation / EANS / European Stroke Journal
summary: This GRADE guideline updates spontaneous ICH management across 37 clinical questions. It favors stroke-unit care and advises against using the ICH score alone to determine prognosis. For minor-to-moderate ICH, it suggests early controlled systolic BP lowering below 140 mmHg while avoiding excessive reductions.
whyItMatters: Use a coordinated ICH pathway and early specialist input. Avoid blanket treatment-limitation policies in the first 24 hours; individual patient wishes and clinical context remain essential.
limitations: Many recommendations are weak or consensus-based. BP guidance is most applicable to hematomas <30 mL and does not establish benefit for every severe or surgical ICH.
population: Adults with spontaneous, nontraumatic intracerebral hemorrhage.
comparator: Prior 2014 ESO guidance and usual care.
primaryEndpoint: Mortality, dependence and other critical clinical outcomes.
findings: The BP consensus advises avoiding a fall >70 mmHg from baseline or actively lowering systolic BP below 110 mmHg.
Stroke-unit care is strongly recommended for patients who do not require intensive care.
evidenceNotes: Historical backfill. Primary open-access guideline abstract, methods and relevant recommendation table sections on stroke-unit care, BP and prognosis reviewed; not every supplement or recommendation was appraised. Electronic date May 22, 2025 verified from PubMed XML. This is European guidance; local US protocols may differ.
guidelineStrength: Stroke-unit care: strong/moderate certainty. Acute BP targets and early prognostic cautions include expert consensus; many other recommendations are weak.
